title: Parameters, custom dimensions and metrics, user properties
reading_md:
## What it is

Every event carries parameters that describe it. `page_location` says which page an event happened on, and `value` says what an action was worth. Some parameters arrive automatically; you can also send your own with any event.

Sending is not reporting. A custom parameter you send does arrive in GA4, but you cannot choose it in reports or explorations until you register it as a custom definition, on the Custom definitions screen in Admin. Registration is not retroactive: a new custom dimension shows data from the moment you register it, and never earlier.

The scope says what the value describes.

- **Event scope:** one action. Voltmarkt's webshop sends `stock_status` ("in stock" or "backorder") with each product page view, so it becomes an event-scoped custom dimension.
- **User scope:** the person, carried onto their later activity. It starts as a user property, such as `preferred_store`, which you then register with user scope.
- **Item scope:** one product inside an ecommerce event's list of items, such as an `energy_label` for each TV in an order.
- **Custom metric:** a number you want to add up or average, such as a `discount_eur` parameter on the `purchase` event, registered as a custom metric rather than a dimension.

**Limits.** For a standard property, with Analytics 360 in brackets: 50 (125) event-scoped custom dimensions, 25 (100) user-scoped custom dimensions, 10 (25) item-scoped custom dimensions, and 50 (125) custom metrics. These limits are one reason to register only the parameters you will actually report on.

## What the exam asks

- **Choosing the scope.** Ask what the value would describe if you read it on its own. A page, a click or an order points to event scope. A customer points to user scope. A product inside an order points to item scope.
- **Why a parameter is missing from reports.** When a scenario says a parameter is being sent but cannot be found in reports, check three things in order. Was it registered as a custom definition? Was it registered with the right scope for what it describes? Was it registered only recently? Data from before registration never appears.

## Common confusions

- Sending a parameter is not the same as registering it.
- A user property is about the person, not one action. An attribute of a single page view belongs in event scope, even when it looks like a property of the person.
- Registering a dimension today does not fill in last month.
- A custom metric holds numbers. A text value, such as a name or a label, is a custom dimension.
- Avoid high-cardinality values, such as timestamps, that are different on nearly every event. Too many unique values make GA4 group the rare rows into a single "(other)" row.
